name: Threads of Time, a textile exhibition
description_text:
Thames Valley Contemporary Textiles is a group of interesting and diverse members, who combined - have an immense range of experience and talents from traditional crafts to contemporary textiles. Our mission as a group is to learn from each other, be progressive and forward thinking but most importantly keeping the traditional crafts alive and passing these amazing skills and techniques onto the next generation.
‘Threads of Time’ is an intimate exhibition of mixed media and textile work inspired by the personal, symbolic and cultural connections to an artefact resulting in a modern interpretation. Artefacts can be powerful non-verbal storytellers, to educate and express personal experiences to a place, a time and society thus inspiring a diverse range of ideas and outcomes.
Open daily, 10am - 4pm
Free admission

name: Live Poetry At Riverhouse - November
description_text:
Live Poetry at Riverhouse, our monthly series bringing the spoken word to the warm, intimate setting of the Barn stage, returns with more guest poets of national standing who’ll read and discuss their work, plus the ever popular Open Mic spots, where you have the chance to read your own work to a friendly, appreciative audience! The evenings are once again hosted by Riverhouse Poets tutor Katie Griffiths.
In this month’s event, Katie will be in conversation with headliners Jacqueline Saphra and John McCullough , both prize-winning poets whose work fearlessly embraces vital modern themes.
Jacqueline Saphra is a poet, playwright, librettist and activist. She is the author of nine plays, five chapbooks and five poetry collections. Her second collection, All My Mad Mothers (Nine Arches Press) was shortlisted for the TS Eliot Prize. Her fifth, Velvel’s Violin , a Poetry Book Society Recommendation and Radio 4 Poetry Book of the month, was published by Nine Arches Press in July 2023 and her sixth collection will be out in 2027. She teaches for The Poetry School and is a founder member of Poets for The Planet.
John McCullough lives in Hove. His book of poems, Reckless Paper Birds (Penned in the Margins) won the 2020 Hawthornden Prize for Literature as well as being shortlisted for the Costa Poetry Award. John’s collections have been Books of the Year for publications including The Guardian, The Times, The Independent and The Telegraph and he also won the Polari First Book Prize. The poem ‘Flower of Sulphur’, from his fourth collection Panic Response (Penned in the Margins), was shortlisted for the 2021 Forward Prize for Best Single Poem. His fifth collection, Crowd Voltage , was published in March 2026 by Bloodaxe.
Katie Griffiths is author of The Attitudes and Mindset Mindrise (Nine Arches Press) and the prize-winning My Shrink is Pregnant (Live Canon). She came second in 2018’s National Poetry Competition, and in 2024 won the Gregory O’Donoghue International Poetry Prize. She regularly mentors, and leads poetry workshops including here at Riverhouse.

name: CHRISTMAS Lunchtime Concert - A Christmas Carol: a musical drama (‘melodrama’) for narrator, violin and piano
tickets: Admission £18.00; Disabled £18.00; Concert Lunch at 11:30am (in the café) £16.00; Concert Lunch at 14:00 (in the café) £16.00
description_text:
Join us for a special lunchtime narrated concert as A Christmas Carol is brought to life through words and music by Leora Cohen on violin, Paul Wingfield on piano and narrator Sophie Max. This spell-binding performance combines story and music in a unique way.
A Christmas Carol: a musical drama (‘melodrama’) for narrator, violin and piano
Charles Dickens ’ beloved Ghost story of Christmas is recreated as a musical drama, in which the narrative is spoken to the accompaniment of music for violin and piano. This genre, called ‘melodrama’ in the nineteenth century, was immensely popular throughout Europe when Dickens was alive. The show, lasting about seventy minutes, has a script abridged from the original 1843 novella and a score by Paul Wingfield, composer of the hugely successful melodrama Einstein’s Violin, which tells the story of the great scientist’s life as a musician.
The score incorporates references to Victorian Christmas music and is immersed in Dickens’ own musical world: Dickens was a great devotee of nineteenth-century supernatural operas, of which his particular favourite was Gounod’s Faust. This vibrant re-imagining of Dickens’ novella thus both transports to the listener to the author’s own cultural surroundings and provides an original perspective on a timeless literary classic.
Performers:
Leora Cohen (violin)
Leora Cohen, alumna of Channing School, Cambridge University and the Royal College of Music, enjoys a diverse career as a recitalist, soloist, and ensemble musician around the world. Having led concerts in major halls globally, and concert series such as the BBC Proms, she now plays as a regular soloist with professional orchestras as well as recitals across the UK and Germany.
Paul Wingfield (piano)
Paul Wingfield was trained at Chetham's School of Music, where he studied the oboe, piano and composition. After an active performing career, Paul pursued a career as an academic at Trinity College, Cambridge where he is the Director of Studies in Music and Secretary of the Council. He has come out of semi-retirement as a musician to accompany Leora Cohen as part of a duo giving concerts around the UK.
Sophie Max (narrator)
Sophie Max is a British-Austrian actor and writer who trained at the American Academy of Dramatic Arts in New York and the Royal Central School of Speech and Drama. Screen includes: We Were The Lucky Ones (Hulu/Disney+), Silent Witness (BBC) and The Whole Truth. Stage includes: Jessica in The Merchant of Venice, Phebe in As You Like It (New York), Helena in A Midsummer Night's Dream (off-Broadway) and Michelle in Nowhere Man (off-Broadway, originated role). As a screenwriter, Sophie is developing a variety of original television and film projects. As a playwright: her debut play, Til It Stops, was Longlisted for the Women's Prize for Playwriting & RSC’s 37 Plays Project and Shortlisted for Bold Playwrights; Banned was part of a showcase of new women writers at the Bush Theatre and subsequently premiered at the Hope Theatre. She is a participant of the Royal Court Writers’ Group. Sophie is represented as an actor by the Narrow Road Company and as a screenwriter by Casarotto Ramsay & Associates.
Reviews
“It was a lovely evening... engagingly presented and put together with a real sense of creative partnership between the performers. It kept everyone’s attention throughout and as they left the audience had clearly really enjoyed it.” Katherine Ives, Director of Lauderdale House, London
“It was absolutely delightful. The costumes, the dazzling performances, the stunning originality of the whole idea. I've never before been present at any performance of anything where the entire audience smiled the whole way through.” Vivienne Brown, audience
“What a wonderful way to spend a summer evening. The charming trio totally looked the part and played their roles with conviction, humour and great musicality. I almost felt as if I were in Mrs Bennett’s drawing room, spellbound by those familiar words and captivated by the superb musical performances” Mary Blackman, audience
“It is a charming programme - a perfect evening’s entertainment” Andrew McRobb, costume designer
“The three performers...each with impressive bios, were certainly in possession of talent and didn’t want for a more appreciative audience. A delight from start to finish. Sophie Max beautifully narrating Gill Hornby’s abridged version of the original text... accompanied by Leora and Paul expertly playing Carl Davis’ score on violin and piano respectively. An inspired coming together of the performing arts. The Regency costumes and mini-staging... were an extra bonus” Shelley-Anne Salisbury, review in the ‘Suburb News’

name: Mock Tudor Comedy Club - December
description_text:
With headliner DOMINIC HOLLAND , plus the return of the fantastic MC, CERYS NELMES along with the very funny ALEX MITCHELL and introducing FREYA MALLARD !
Award-winning comedian, author, and broadcaster DOMINIC HOLLAND is one of the UK’s most respected and versatile comic talents. With a career spanning stand-up, television, radio, and writing, Dominic has built a reputation for sharp observational humour delivered with intelligence, warmth, and impeccable timing. Dominic first rose to prominence after winning the prestigious Perrier Best Newcomer Award at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, marking him out as a major force on the UK comedy circuit. Since then, he has become a regular headliner at leading comedy venues across the country and internationally, known for his polished performances and effortlessly engaging stage presence.
A familiar voice and face across British media, Dominic has appeared on numerous television and radio programmes, as well as writing and performing his own critically acclaimed shows. His work combines wit and insight, often drawing on family life, modern relationships, and the absurdities of everyday living.
TV credits include Have I Got News For You, The Royal Variety Performance, Never Mind the Buzzcocks, The Stand Up Show (BBC), They Think It’s All Over, plus appearances on Richard & Judy, This Morning, and The One Show.
Despite his considerable efforts and many successes in comedy, Dominic admits that his greatest achievement in life is being a father to 4 boys — most notably to his eldest son, actor Tom Holland — a reality that inspired his bestselling non-fiction book Eclipsed.
Our MC, CERYS NELMES , returns by popular demand having stormed her last two appearances with us! Cerys is a highly entertaining British stand-up comedian, award-winning MC, actress, and TV warm-up artist originating from the Cotswolds. Known for her cheerful West Country charm, sharp storytelling, and flawless audience interaction.
Also featuring on the bill is ALEX MITCHELL - an award-winning stand-up comedian, writer, actor and podcaster who has become one of the most exciting and distinctive new voices on the UK comedy circuit. Just eighteen months after his first open mic, Alex reached the final of Britain’s Got Talent. The following year he was a finalist in the prestigious Leicester Square Theatre New Comedian of the Year competition. Since then he has become a regular at many of the UK’s biggest comedy venues, performing in clubs and theatres including The Stand, Glee, Up the Creek, Backyard and Komedia Brighton, and, now, Mock Tudor Comedy! Alex is queer, autistic and disabled, and much of his work draws on these experiences. He has written and performed two critically acclaimed solo shows which sold out at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in 2024 and 2025, toured across the UK, appeared on Rosie Jones’ Disability Comedy Extravaganza, Good Morning Britain, Lorraine, NextUp Comedy and Heart Radio, and provided tour support for Hal Cruttenden. Alex has fast become a favourite with audiences across the UK.
And introducing FREYA MALLARD - an English stand-up comedian, actor and writer known for her silly, smart and slightly absurd take on modern life. A regular performer across the UK comedy circuit, Freya has appeared at the Edinburgh Fringe, Glastonbury and Brighton Fringe, as well as on ITV2’s The Stand Up Sketch Show and BBC radio and comedy programming. Her work has also built a significant online following, with millions of likes across social media platforms. Freya was shortlisted for the BBC New Comedy Award and named a Funny Women Awards One to Watch, alongside being a Leicester Square New Comedian finalist. Her debut Edinburgh show received critical acclaim, including a four-star for ‘ The Bounce Back’ .

description_text:
Join Oliver Darley and Chad LeLong (the team that brought you Simply Bowie, Simply George Michael and Simply Freddie), for an intimate evening of timeless songs from the Great American Songbook , brought to life with nothing more than voice, piano and a shared love of great music.
Described by Tony Bennett as " America’s classical music ”, we roam from the wit and sophistication of Cole Porter to the romance of Gershwin, Berlin and Rodgers & Hart . Enduring classics, such as ‘Moon River’, ‘Summertime’ and ‘White Christmas’ are given fresh, personal interpretations.
Expect beautiful melodies, sparkling lyrics, swinging rhythms and extraordinary back stories that still resonate today. Stripped back to their essence, these timeless little moments in musical history reveal just why they have captivated audiences for generations. A warm, elegant and seasonal celebration of some of the greatest songs ever written.

description_text:

From gift-giving and pine trees to Santa Claus and reindeer, Christmas is one of the most ubiquitously celebrated holidays on earth. And yet its origins and its millennia-long journey to become the holiday season we know today may surprise you. To learn more about how Indian bull deities, Roman decadence and Christian controversies shaped the holiday of Christmas, join Tim Hazell, Riverhouse’s Historian in Residence, and unwrap the ancient history behind the festive season!

name: 'We Are Like That Only!'
description_text:
A photographic journey of 14 years through the streets of Mumbai by Constantine
'For more than a decade, I have roamed many Indian streets and markets. Unlike my fellow westerners, I fell in love with everything but the Taj, yoga retreats, or majestic Rajasthan. I left beautiful India to the tourists without imagination, for I find the beauty of India in the everydayness of city life. In its contradictions, I find the harsh realities of daily toil, the kindness, the cruelty, the endeavour, and the willingness to embrace tomorrow's unknowns, as a motive for overcoming today's struggles. Nothing stops me from venturing into the orchestrated chaos of India's city streets because that that is where life Is. So this is what I try to capture... We are like that only!’
For some, photography is a hobby. For others a profession. Some love the tech, some enjoy the outdoors. Others record stuff, like babies being born, and people getting married. Some document crime scenes and dissect the pixel to discover who did what to whom. Some do surveys... too many if you ask me.
Some use it as a form of expression with artistic endeavours, I shoot people.
It feeds my Curiosity, and my Passion to see the world around me in a frame.
Taking every day and giving it importance. It brings me a sense of Intimacy through the immersion into the lives of people and it is a vehicle of discovery and understanding without words.
A street photograph is a conversation with a friend.

Free admission

name: Storytelling of dreams, by Konstantinos: A retrospective of 20 years in 30 paintings
description_text:
The artist is self-taught. He works in oil on canvas-lined board, mostly around 60 × 100 cm.
Greece, India and England are where he grew up, lived and worked. He knows how each place smells and tastes. They meet on canvas because they have already mingled in his mind. He paints intuitively. Deliberation comes later and is fitted in where it will go. His work is allegorical figuration in the metaphysical tradition. For him, metaphysical means that everything happens at once: the now sits inside the then, and the then is built from what the now knows. His main influences are Giorgio de Chirico, Alberto Savinio, Engonopoulos, Óscar Domínguez, Fritz Kahn and Gautier d'Agoty for his anatomical references.
He uses distorted space and deliberately unresolved perspective to create unease, tension and intrigue. He says he regularly gets bored doing one kind of painting. When that happens, he pushes into styles outside his comfort zone. He wants the work to be a conversation with the viewer, a discussion, even an argument. For him, it is the only way to discover the new, the fresh, the different.

name: Lunchtime concert - Duality, Four Hands on One Keyboard Emma Abbate & Julian Perkins
description_text:
As passionate advocates for the rich repertory for Four Hands on One Keyboard, Emma Abbate and Julian Perkins perform widely, with appearances for the Mozart's Society of America and at many UK venues, including the Royal Opera House Covent Garden, St George's Bristol, Sinfonia Smith Square, Hatchlands Park and St Cecilia's hall in Edinburgh.
Praised for their 'impressive sensitivity' ( Early Music reviews ) and for telling a 'totally convincing stoory with every piece' ( The Arts Desk ), their recordings have received 5-star reviews in BBC Music Magazine and Het Nieuwsblad.
Their varied discography include Mozart's complete sonatas for keyboard duet on period instruments, Weber's Complete Keyboard Duets on an original Viennese fortepiano, as well as Tournamant for Twenty Fingers featuring works by British composers from the twentieth century.
Their latest disc is Summer Dreams , which brings together the complete works for piano duet by 3 American composers: Edward MacDowell, Amy Beach and Samuel Barber. This was Album of the Week at Radio 3 Berlin-Brandenburg.
Emma & Julian have been each elected Associates of the Royal Academy of Music in recognition for their 'significant contribution' thus far to the music profession.
Programme:
Wilhelm Friederich Ernst Bach, Duet no. 2 in G Major
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Sonata for piano four hands in C Major, K. 521
Franz Schubert, Allegro in A Minor for piano four hands, D. 947, Op. 144, Lebenssturme
Peter Warlock, Capriol Suite

name: Royston Pike Lectures- Musical Encounters: Of Humans and Machines with Milton Mermikides (Jan 2027)
description_text:
From ninth-century musical automata in Baghdad and the first recorded human voice to the 200-ton electrically powered synthesizers of the 1890s, the history of machines making music is far older than we might imagine.
In this engaging, richly illustrated lecture, Milton Mermikides explores the fascinating relationship between human creativity and technology. From mechanical musicians and early sound recordings to electronic instruments, digital revolutions and artificial intelligence, discover how each innovation has transformed the way we create, perform and experience music.
Through stories, demonstrations and musical examples, Milton explores our growing relationship with technology, asking where human creativity ends and machine collaboration begins – and what this might mean for the future of music.
Milton Mermikides is a composer, guitarist and academic whose work explores the connections between music, science and technology. The son of a CERN nuclear physicist, he has collaborated with leading musicians and scientists, with his work featured in major academic publications and international media. He is Professor of Music at the University of Surrey, Professor of Jazz Guitar at the Royal College of Music, and the 37th Gresham Professor of Music, a historic public lectureship founded in 1597.
Presented by Elmbridge Borough Council in association with Riverhouse Barn Arts Centre

description_text:
Following his successful charity concerts Stepping Out and Stepping Up at the Riverhouse Barn, Andy Mais is now Stepping Off – inviting you to share an evening of classical and contemporary piano playing and songs.
To start 2027, join Andy for a relaxed, informal and entertaining evening of classical and contemporary piano music, songs and perhaps a few surprises along the way. Who knows, it might even rekindle your own enthusiasm for making music!
The programme will include classical favourites by Beethoven and Rachmaninov, alongside a wide range of contemporary music, from Ed Sheeran to Tim Minchin. There will also be some jazz, improvisation and original compositions, reflecting Andy's growing enthusiasm for exploring new musical territory.
Andy is a classically trained amateur pianist who is venturing into improvisation, jazz and singing. He played in several bands at university and moved to London in his twenties working as an engineer in the Construction industry. During this time he hosted several small charity concerts and really enjoyed bringing new performers together. Now several decades later and a dad to 3 young adults, his passion is to encourage adults to take up the piano, expand his classical repertoire and sing and play more in public sometimes well outside his comfort zone. He can sometimes be seen playing on public pianos in train stations and airports on his way to different cities and countries with his work.
Andy is delighted that all proceeds from the evening will support two charities close to his heart ANDYSMANCLUB – It's Okay To Talk and The Amber Trust .

Life Drawing and Art Nude Photography.
The exhibition can be taken at face value and can be appreciated or rejected at its aesthetic level or competence of skill.
Its true purpose however is to offer a challenge, which the visitor may wish to consider and it is this,
Is one objectifying and the other celebrating?
Is one emancipation and the other servitude?
Is one the result of observation and the other of voyeurism?
Am I appreciating or am I consuming?
The answers are with the viewer. You are invited to consider, contemplate and debate.
Open daily 10am - 4pm
Free admission
16+ at parental discretion

name: Lunchtime Concert - Elmore Quartet
description_text:
Winners of the 74th Royal Over-Seas League Annual Music Competition, the Elmore Quartet is a young British Quartet based in London.
Over the past two years, the Elmore Quartet have recorded multiple times for BBC Radio 3 and performed at esteemed venues throughout the UK and Europe, including Wigmore Hall, Kings Place London, Brighton Dome and Bridgewater Hall. In 2024, they were awarded Third Prize at the 13th edition of the Premio Paolo Borciani International String Quartet Competition in Reggio Emilia, Italy.
Their successes include awards from the Tunnell Trust and the Kirckman Concert Society Award, opportunities which brought the Quartet to audiences across the UK, including the beautiful Scottish Highlands. In 2025, they joined the prestigious network of Italy's Le Dimore del Quartetto upon invitation and in 2026 were invited to join the roster of Philip and Dorothy Green Young Artist, in addition to being appointed Chamber Studio Fellows.
In 2024, the Elmores were selected as Penzance MusicAbility Foundation's first resident String Quartet in partnership with the Frost Trust. This four-year position allows the Quartet to integrate themselves into West Cornwall's unique community by performing regularly as part of the Concerts Penzance concert series, working with local schools, and utilising their passion for sharing classical music with new audiences.
Previously, the Quartet held the position of Hans Keller Chamber Fellows at the Guildhall School of Music and Drama, following a Fellowship position at the Royal Northern College of Music where they taught chamber music to Undergraduate and Postgraduate students in Manchester, where the Quartet was formed.

name: PINOCCHIO
tickets: Adult £14.00; Disabled Adult £14.00; Disabled Child under 12 £10.00; Child under 12 £10.00; Under 2 years old not taking a seat £0.00
description_text:
Steve Tiplady, as Geppetto, uses the objects of a carpenter’s workshop to tell the tale of the puppet that wants to be a real boy, and the puppet-maker who wants to be a real father.
Pinocchio is carved on stage, brushes become a fox and the shadow of two saws transforms into a giant shark. An element of improvisation makes each performance unique to its audience.
Puppetry, shadows, illusion and especially composed music combine to create a show with something for all ages; it’s inventive, visually and verbally witty with a big heart.
“Wonderful work that celebrates the possibilities of theatre” Lyn Gardner, The Guardian
“Truly magical...captivating...hauntingly real” The Scotsman

name: Royston Pike Lectures: County Herb Committees with Our Plant Stories (Feb 2027)
description_text:
During the Second World War, trade restrictions meant that medical supplies were in short supply, so the British government set up County Herb Committees to coordinate the gathering, drying and processing of wild medicinal herbs. Volunteers from the Women’s Institute as well as Scouts and school children were enlisted to help. In Surrey, collectors were paid 2d per oz for foxglove seeds and 3d per lb for rose hips, and Surrey History Centre holds records of the local campaign and people who contributed. This is a fascinating and perhaps forgotten story of the war effort. In a panel conversation, we’ll learn what was being collected and why, including how the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, were also involved.
Chairing the panel will be Sally Flatman, a former BBC Radio 4 producer. In her podcast, Our Plant Stories, she digs into the stories that plants tell us about people and places. The Times described it as “pick of the gardening podcasts”. Other guest panellists will include Kayleigh Sinclair, ‘The Historical Herbologist’, who frequently gives talks at RHS Wisley. This discussion will be recorded for a future podcast episode.

name: Royston Pike Lectures: The Library: a brief history of books and the buildings that house them  (Mar 2027)
description_text:
The Library: a brief history of books and the buildings that house them with James W.P. Campbell
Library architecture has often served as a striking symbol of a society’s creativity, means, and ambition for learning. Drawing from the landmark book The Library: A World History, this talk explores how cultures from ancient Mesopotamia to modern China have reinvented these sacred spaces across the globe. Join us to discover how the design and atmosphere of some of the world’s iconic libraries reflect human priorities and mirror the story of civilization itself.
James W.P. Campbell is an architect and architectural historian with a particular passion for books and libraries. He is a Professor in the University of Cambridge where he has taught for the last twenty years and is the Seear Fellow in Architecture and History of Art of Queens’ College. He is author of The Library: A World History, available in 12 languages.
This talk is arranged as a special tribute to Edgar Royston Pike! Author, historian and former Chairman of Esher Council, Edgar launched this series in the late 1960s, then known as the 'Esher Library Lectures’. Elmbridge Borough Council later re-named it to celebrate his 20 dedicated years on the Library Committee. His work made knowledge accessible by championing community library education, illuminating everyday human experiences and exploring economic history, world faiths, ancient civilisations and rational thought.
Presented by Elmbridge Borough Council in association with Riverhouse Barn Arts Centre

name: Mother's Day Concert -Violetta Suvini (Violin), Salome Jordania (Piano)
description_text:
Programme:
Ravel Sonate Posthume
Lili Boulanger D'un Matin de Printemps
Dvorak Songs My Mother Taught Me
Dora Pejačević ' Spring' sonata
Irish-Italian violinist Violetta Suvini is acclaimed as “an artist of great originality and vision”. A versatile recitalist and chamber musician, she is a City Music Foundation Artist for 2025–27 and winner of the Royal Philharmonic Society’s Emily Anderson Prize in 2024.
Violetta has performed at prestigious venues and festivals including Wigmore Hall, the Barbican, Aldeburgh and the Venice Biennale. A passionate advocate for contemporary music, she has given 16 world premieres and commissioned works by emerging composers. She is a founding member of the innovative Komuna Collective, and was also a Britten Pears Young Artist in 2024–25.
Violetta graduated with distinction from the Guildhall School of Music and Drama in 2023, having previously achieved First Class Honours at Oxford.
Georgian pianist Salome Jordania has performed internationally as a recitalist, chamber musician and concerto soloist, appearing at prestigious venues and festivals across Europe, the United States and beyond. A prize winner in more than thirty international competitions, she was the sole winner of the New York Concert Artists Competition, leading to her acclaimed debut at Berlin’s Philharmonie in 2023.
A passionate collaborator, Salome has worked with leading contemporary composers, including Pulitzer Prize winners John Corigliano and Jennifer Higdon. Recent highlights include her debut at Amsterdam’s Concertgebouw Grand Hall with the trio The Graces, and a duo recital at Wigmore Hall with bassist Strahinja Mitrović.
Salome holds degrees from The Juilliard School and Yale School of Music and recently completed the Artist Diploma programme at London’s Guildhall School of Music and Drama, where she was a Steinway & Sons Scholar.

name: Lunchtime Concert -  Wren Piano Trio
description_text:
Wren Piano Trio with Richard Uttley (piano), Nathaniel Anderson-Frank (violin) and Ella Rundle (cello)
Having performed together in various chamber music collaborations over many years—including recitals at Wigmore Hall—these three distinguished musicians have now come together as the Wren Piano Trio. The trio draws on extensive experience as soloists and chamber musicians, combining technical assurance with expressive depth and musical spontaneity. Their performances have been praised for their “unfazed expertise” (Classical Source), “assiduous clarity, lyrical poise” and “dashing” playing (The Times). Recent engagements include performances across the UK and at the Fête Musicale de la Forêt in Argonne, France.
Leader of the BBC Concert Orchestra, Nathaniel Anderson-Frank’s playing has been praised for its “suaveness and depth of tone” (The Arts Desk). He is frequently featured as soloist with the Concert Orchestra and was previously a member of the prize-winning Piatti Quartet. Noted for her “infectious passion” (Ottawa Citizen), Ella Rundle is an accomplished soloist and chamber musician. A member of the Philharmonia Orchestra, she regularly plays as guest principal with leading UK orchestras. Richard Uttley has given solo and chamber recitals at many of the most prestigious venues and festivals internationally, and is a piano professor at the Royal College of Music in London.

name: Andrew Ryan: Honest Capacity
description_text:
Off the back of a total sell-out tour in 2024, Andrew Ryan is back with a brand-new show. Everyone’s favourite Cork in the North returns in good faith and in an honest capacity with what promises to be his biggest and most hilarious show to date.
On the face of it Andrew is utterly delighted with himself these days; he’s happy, confident, can drive a golf ball 300 yards and is excited for the future as a newlywed. Barely touch that surface and the reality is he cannot get out of his own way and continues to make utterly bewildering decisions with hilarious consequences. Join him for his new show with tales of pet ownership, constant inability to read a room, and his unrelenting frustration and annoyance with the world around him. Everything is fine, until it’s not!
Host of the Q Radio Breakfast Show and Star of The Two Jonnies Late Night Lock In (RTE), The Blame Game (BBC), Comedy Central Live, along with hit appearances on some of the biggest comedy podcasts in the UK and Ireland. He is a frequent viral hit with over 50 million views amassed across social media.
“Charming, Hilarious with some really powerful thinking underneath” - The Metro
“Well paced, well written, delivers plenty of laughs” - The Mirror
“Ferociously intelligent, Ryan is a great writer. Charming, hilarious and accessible with some really powerful thinking underneath it all.” - The Skinny

name: Harbottle & Jonas
description_text:
Partners in life and music, dynamic Devon-based duo Harbottle & Jonas are one of the most exciting acts on the UK folk circuit today. They seamlessly blend the richness of traditional folk with their own original and powerful songwriting, creating a distinct and compelling signature sound.
Blending concertina, harmonium, banjo, stomp box, acoustic guitar, and cittern – and their beautiful, closely intertwined vocal harmonies, Dave and Freya captivate audiences with every performance.
Their songs explore historical tales and personal narratives, weaving stories into their live shows that are as engaging as they are moving. Through their intimate and timeless music, Harbottle & Jonas bring people, places, and events vividly to life.
"The legendary Harbottle and Jonas... incredible" – BBC 6 Music
"… like a cosmic, contemporary Fairport Convention" – The Guardian

name: Jazz Sabbath
description_text:
Jazz Sabbath are back at Riverhouse!
Led by 2026 Grammy-winning pianist Adam Wakeman (keys for Black Sabbath and Ozzy Osbourne since 2004), Jazz Sabbath is a jazz trio from Great Britain that plays new jazz arrangements of Black Sabbath songs, although the band presents itself as a jazz trio founded in 1968 and the original authors of the tracks later made famous by Black Sabbath.
Jazz Sabbath explores the boundaries between jazz and the songs that defined heavy metal, revisiting existing jazz riffs and discovering new ones. Whether or not you choose to believe their wild backstory, with three albums high in the Billboard Jazz Charts, sold-out shows worldwide, and rave reviews in both jazz and rock media, Jazz Sabbath is quickly making its way (back) to the top of the jazz scene.
'Surprisingly superb' - Jazz Journal
'Absolutely terrific' - Jazzwise
'Never has heavy metal been so groovy' - MetalTalk
'Spectacular renditions' - Metal Injection
'Amazing interpretations' - Tony Iommi
